records.context: **A file that exists is not a file that finished.** Older versions of ``spacr.io._load_and_concatenate_arrays`` wrote ``merged/<field>.npy`` with a bare ``np.save`` straight onto the destination path, so a crash mid-write left a short, structurally valid-looking ``.npy`` on disk. Current versions write merged arrays atomically, but files left by earlier runs can still be truncated. A resume that skips on ``os.path.exists`` would accept such a field, measure whatever bytes happened to land, and put the result in the same table as the good fields. So :func:`completed_fields_in_merged` *validates*: it parses the ``.npy`` header and checks that the file is as long as its own shape claims. Anything short is reported as rejected and re-queued, never skipped.
records.label: spacr.resume#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A file that exists is not a file that finished.** Older versions of ``spacr.io._load_and_concatenate_arrays`` wrote ``merged/<field>.npy`` with a bare ``np.save`` straight onto the destination path, so a crash mid-write left a short, structurally valid-looking ``.npy`` on disk. Current versions write merged arrays atomically, but files left by earlier runs can still be truncated. A resume that skips on ``os.path.exists`` would accept such a field, measure whatever bytes happened to land, and put the result in the same table as the good fields. So :func:`completed_fields_in_merged` *validates*: it parses the ``.npy`` header and checks that the file is as long as its own shape claims. Anything short is reported as rejected and re-queued, never skipped.
records.translation: **Um arquivo que existe não é um arquivo concluído.** Versões antigas de ``spacr.io._load_and_concatenate_arrays`` gravavam ``merged/<field>.npy`` com um simples ``np.save`` diretamente no caminho de destino, de modo que uma falha no meio da gravação deixava no disco um ``.npy`` curto, com estrutura aparentemente válida. As versões atuais gravam as matrizes mescladas de forma atômica, mas arquivos deixados por execuções anteriores ainda podem estar truncados. Uma retomada que pulasse campos com base em ``os.path.exists`` aceitaria esse campo, mediria os bytes que por acaso foram gravados e colocaria o resultado na mesma tabela que os campos íntegros. Por isso :func:`completed_fields_in_merged` *valida*: interpreta o cabeçalho do ``.npy`` e verifica se o arquivo tem o comprimento que sua própria forma declara. Qualquer arquivo curto é informado como rejeitado e recolocado na fila, nunca pulado.

records.context: **The measurement workflow appends rows, so existing rows must be removed prior to continuing an interrupted run.** ``_merge_and_save_to_database`` and ``filepaths_to_database`` both call ``to_sql(..., if_exists='append')``. Measuring a field again does not replace existing rows; it *inserts additional rows*. This makes downstream per-well aggregates too large without a warning. :func:`clear_field_rows` removes old rows so repeated measurement produces one consistent result. One transaction covers every affected table, so an error leaves the database unchanged.
records.label: spacr.resume#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Measure appends; therefore a resume must delete first.** ``_merge_and_save_to_database`` and ``filepaths_to_database`` both use ``to_sql(..., if_exists='append')``. Re-measuring a field that already wrote some rows does not overwrite them, it *adds* to them, and every per-well aggregate downstream is then computed over inflated counts with nothing anywhere to indicate it. :func:`clear_field_rows` is the delete-before-insert that makes re-running a field idempotent, and it is the reason this module exists at all. It runs in one transaction across every table the field touched, so a failure part-way leaves the database exactly as it was.
records.translation: **A medição acrescenta linhas; portanto, uma retomada precisa apagar primeiro.** ``_merge_and_save_to_database`` e ``filepaths_to_database`` usam ambas ``to_sql(..., if_exists='append')``. Medir de novo um campo que já gravou algumas linhas não as sobrescreve, mas *acrescenta* a elas, e todo agregado por poço calculado depois passa a usar contagens infladas, sem nada que o indique. :func:`clear_field_rows` é a exclusão antes da inserção que torna idempotente a nova execução de um campo, e é a razão de este módulo existir. Ela é executada em uma única transação sobre todas as tabelas que o campo afetou, de modo que uma falha no meio deixa o banco de dados exatamente como estava.

records.context: **measurements.db is not measure's private file.** ``convert`` writes ``conversion_map`` into it, ``align`` writes ``align_coordinates``, ``foreign`` writes ``foreign_*``, ``timelapse`` writes its track table — all keyed on the same four columns as the measurements, deliberately, so that they join. Discovering "tables to clear" by their columns alone would therefore find all of them, and clearing a pending microscope field of view from each would delete the only record of which vendor file became ``plate1_A01_1``, of where each microscope image field was stitched, and of imported measurements. None of it can be recomputed from the database. The tables a resume may delete from are therefore an explicit allow-list, :data:`MEASURE_OWNED_TABLES`, checked both when the list is discovered and again per table immediately before the DELETE is prepared.
records.label: spacr.resume#5

records.source: **measurements.db is not measure's private file.** ``convert`` writes ``conversion_map`` into it, ``align`` writes ``align_coordinates``, ``foreign`` writes ``foreign_*``, ``timelapse`` writes its track table — all keyed on the same four columns as the measurements, deliberately, so that they join. Discovering "tables to clear" by their columns alone would therefore find all of them, and clearing a pending field from each would delete the only record of which vendor file became ``plate1_A01_1``, of where each tile was stitched, and of imported measurements. None of it can be recomputed from the database. The tables a resume may delete from are therefore an explicit allow-list, :data:`MEASURE_OWNED_TABLES`, checked both when the list is discovered and again per table immediately before the DELETE is prepared.
records.translation: **measurements.db não é um arquivo exclusivo da medição.** ``convert`` grava ``conversion_map`` nele, ``align`` grava ``align_coordinates``, ``foreign`` grava ``foreign_*`` e ``timelapse`` grava sua tabela de trajetórias — todas indexadas pelas mesmas quatro colunas das medições, de propósito, para que possam ser unidas. Descobrir as tabelas a limpar ("tables to clear") apenas pelas colunas encontraria, portanto, todas elas, e limpar um campo pendente de cada uma apagaria o único registro de qual arquivo do fabricante se tornou ``plate1_A01_1``, de onde cada ladrilho foi costurado e das medições importadas. Nenhum desses dados (None of it) pode ser recalculado a partir do banco de dados. Por isso, as tabelas das quais uma retomada pode apagar dados formam uma lista explícita de permissões, :data:`MEASURE_OWNED_TABLES`, verificada tanto quando a lista é descoberta quanto novamente, tabela por tabela, imediatamente antes de o DELETE ser preparado.

records.context: **Owned by name is not owned in fact, so ownership is decided per row.** A name allow-list answers "could measure have written this table?", and there is one case where the answer to "did it?" is no: ``foreign.run_import`` copies the imported rows into the canonical ``cell`` / ``nucleus`` / ``pathogen`` table when nothing of anyone else's is there, so that a purely-imported project is readable by every spaCR tool. Those rows sit under spaCR's own metadata columns in a table on the allow-list, and a table-level rule would clear them along with the pending field.
records.label: spacr.resume#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Owned by name is not owned in fact, so ownership is decided per row.** A name allow-list answers "could measure have written this table?", and there is one case where the answer to "did it?" is no: ``foreign.run_import`` copies the imported rows into the canonical ``cell`` / ``nucleus`` / ``pathogen`` table when nothing of anyone else's is there, so that a purely-imported project is readable by every spaCR tool. Those rows sit under spaCR's own metadata columns in a table on the allow-list, and a table-level rule would clear them along with the pending field.
records.translation: **Pertencer pelo nome não é pertencer de fato, por isso a propriedade é decidida por linha.** Uma lista de permissões por nome responde "a medição poderia ter gravado esta tabela?", e há um caso em que a resposta a "ela gravou?" é não: ``foreign.run_import`` copia as linhas importadas para a tabela canônica ``cell`` / ``nucleus`` / ``pathogen`` quando não há nada de outra origem nela, para que um projeto puramente importado possa ser lido por todas as ferramentas do spaCR. Essas linhas ficam sob as próprias colunas de metadados do spaCR, em uma tabela da lista de permissões, e uma regra no nível da tabela as apagaria junto com o campo pendente.

records.context: The rows are told apart by ``foreign_columns``, written by every release of the importer, names each column that importer put in each table. Its table-scoped use — ``foreign._importer_owns``, "are this table's columns a subset of what the importer recorded?" — has a row-scoped twin, and that is the rule here: **a row is the importer's when every column it is non-NULL in is one the importer recorded for this table**. A ``measure_crop`` row always carries at least its own area and intensity columns, which the importer never wrote; an imported row carries only metadata and ``foreign_``-prefixed measurements. So a table can be half one and half the other and each row is still attributable — which matters, because a project that was imported and then measured is exactly that. See :func:`measure_rows_clause`.

records.source: The rows are told apart by ``foreign_columns``, written by every release of the importer, names each column that importer put in each table. Its table-scoped use — ``foreign._importer_owns``, "are this table's columns a subset of what the importer recorded?" — has a row-scoped twin, and that is the rule here: **a row is the importer's when every column it is non-NULL in is one the importer recorded for this table**. A ``measure_crop`` row always carries at least its own area and intensity columns, which the importer never wrote; an imported row carries only metadata and ``foreign_``-prefixed measurements. So a table can be half one and half the other and each row is still attributable — which matters, because a project that was imported and then measured is exactly that. records.translation: As linhas são distinguidas por ``foreign_columns``, gravada por todas as versões do importador, que nomeia cada coluna que o importador colocou em cada tabela. Seu uso no nível da tabela — ``foreign._importer_owns``, "as colunas desta tabela são um subconjunto do que o importador registrou?" — tem um equivalente no nível da linha, e essa é a regra aqui: **uma linha pertence ao importador quando todas as colunas em que ela não é NULL foram registradas pelo importador para esta tabela**. Uma linha de ``measure_crop`` sempre contém pelo menos suas próprias colunas de área e intensidade, que o importador nunca gravou; uma linha importada contém apenas metadados e medições com o prefixo ``foreign_``. Assim, uma tabela pode ter metade de cada origem e cada linha continua atribuível — o que importa, porque um projeto que foi importado e depois medido é exatamente isso. Consulte :func:`measure_rows_clause`.

records.context: Ownership is not read from a table-level marker such as ``foreign_import.canonical_table_written``. A marker that blocks every delete from a claimed table would also block clearing fields the import never covered, so such a project could never be resumed; and the first importer release wrote the canonical copy without that marker. ``foreign_columns`` is per table and per column, and every importer release has written it.

records.translation: A propriedade não é lida de um marcador no nível da tabela, como ``foreign_import.canonical_table_written``.
